applicable_when: The kernel launches 490 CTAs on 132 SMs (0.23 waves) with XBLOCK=128 and only 4 warps per block (128 threads / 32 threads-per-warp = 4 warps). Each warp does 1 load + 5 strided stores; the L1TEX scoreboard stall (47% of cycles) shows warps are blocked waiting for memory. With only 3.31 active warps/scheduler and 0.30 eligible warps/scheduler, the scheduler has almost nothing to issue. Increasing XBLOCK to 256 (still a multiple of 32) doubles the warp pool per block to 8 warps, giving the scheduler more warps to switch to while others wait on L1TEX. XBLOCK must stay a multiple of 32 because the index decomposition x0 = xindex % 32 / x1 = xindex // 32 requires this for correctness — all three prior attempts that changed XBLOCK to non-multiples-of-32 caused CUDA runtime errors. XBLOCK=256 is safe: 62720 / 256 = 245 CTAs exactly, and 256 % 32 == 0 preserves the index alignment.
